name: Otic ganglion
summary: A small parasympathetic ganglion lying just below the foramen ovale on the medial side of the mandibular nerve, where preganglionic fibers from the inferior salivatory nucleus arriving by the lesser petrosal nerve (glossopharyngeal nerve, via the tympanic plexus) synapse. The postganglionic fibers join the auriculotemporal nerve to reach the parotid gland. Frey syndrome (gustatory sweating over the parotid after parotidectomy) results from aberrant regeneration of these fibers into the sweat glands of the overlying skin.

anatomy.location: Infratemporal fossa immediately below the foramen ovale, medial to the mandibular nerve, lateral to tensor veli palatini and in front of the middle meningeal artery.

function: Relay of parasympathetic secretomotor fibers to the parotid gland; passage of sympathetic fibers from the middle meningeal plexus and of motor fibers to tensor tympani and tensor veli palatini.

bestView.label: infratemporal fossa below the foramen ovale, medial to V3

imaging.normalAppearance: Not identifiable on routine imaging; the foramen ovale and the mandibular nerve are seen on skull base CT and MRI, and perineural spread along V3 passes this region.

pathology.finding: Enlarged enhancing mandibular nerve through the foramen ovale with denervation atrophy of the masticatory muscles.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Skull base MRI with fat saturation

lesionEffects.deficit: Gustatory sweating and flushing over the cheek (Frey syndrome)
lesionEffects.mechanism: Aberrant regeneration of parasympathetic fibers into cutaneous sweat glands after parotid surgery

lesionEffects.deficit: Jaw weakness and V3 numbness with a mass

examination: Observe the cheek during a meal for sweating
Masseter and pterygoid power, V3 sensation
pearls: Sweating over the cheek when eating after parotid surgery is Frey syndrome, a misdirected otic ganglion outflow
The parotid gets its parasympathetic supply from the ninth nerve, not the seventh, despite the facial nerve running through it
